findings.title: Duplicate `def self.downsize` method shadows the original
findings.body: The file ends up with two `def self.downsize` definitions: lines 145–147 keep the 4-arg form `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`, and lines 149–151 add a new 3-arg form `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. Ruby silently redefines the method, so the second definition wins and any caller using `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, width, height)` (the previous public arity) will now raise ArgumentError because the surviving method only accepts three positional arguments. The old definition should have been removed when the new one was added.

findings.title: Client-side upload limit hardcoded to 10 MB, ignoring per-type site setting
findings.body: The previous code used `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, which honored `max_image_size_kb` for images and `max_attachment_size_kb` for attachments. The new code hardcodes `10 * 1024` for every type. This breaks attachment uploads (which have no downsizing fallback server-side) when `max_attachment_size_kb` is below 10 MB, and it can also let through files that the server rejects if `max_image_size_kb` is set below 10 MB. The change is unrelated to the image-downsizing feature and should use the per-type site setting like before.

findings.title: 413 error message always reports 10 MB regardless of configured limit
findings.body: The handler for HTTP 413 now reports `max_size_kb: 10 * 1024` even though the server-side limit comes from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. Users told they exceeded a 10 MB limit will be confused when the actual configured limit is something else (e.g. 1 MB), and the value rendered in the alert no longer reflects the server-side limit that triggered the rejection. The previous `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` value should be preserved here.

findings.title: URL download cap raised to a hardcoded 10 MB, ignoring site setting
findings.body: `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` was replaced with `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`. The cap no longer honors `max_image_size_kb` and is now a fixed 10 MB regardless of what the administrator configured. For sites with a small `max_image_size_kb` this lets callers pull arbitrarily large files into a temp file (only to be downsized afterwards), increasing disk usage and memory pressure. The new 10 MB cap should at minimum remain consistent with `max_image_size_kb` and ideally be configurable.

findings.title: Downsize loop discards `OptimizedImage.downsize` return value
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` can return `false` when ImageMagick fails (e.g. corrupt or unsupported image, even though `FileHelper.is_image?` returned true). The controller ignores the return value, so the loop just decrements `attempt` and keeps going even though the file size never shrinks. There is no logging and no signal to the rest of the flow. The return value should be checked and the failure logged (and ideally surfaced to the user) instead of being silently dropped.

findings.title: Oversized upload proceeds silently after 5 downsize attempts
findings.body: If the file is still larger than `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` after the 5-iteration downsize loop completes, the controller falls through and calls `Upload.create_for` with the still-oversized `tempfile`. There is no error returned, no log entry, and no user-visible message, so a user who uploaded an image expecting it to be resized will get a rejected/oversized upload without explanation. The loop should break out with an explicit error (logged and returned in the response) when downsizing cannot get the file under the configured limit.
